research:
**Rundown: Will Lavrov visit Florida between Nov 30, 2026 and Jan 1, 2027?**

**Current state (as of Nov 24, 2026)**

- **The Florida event:** The G20 leaders' summit is set for Dec. 14–15 at Trump National Doral Golf Club in Miami.
- **Putin's attendance is undecided.** On Nov 24, the Kremlin said a decision on whether Russian President Vladimir Putin will attend the G20 summit in Miami has yet to be made. Peskov said on Nov 18 that the decision would depend on the outcome of Putin's talks with US President Donald Trump in Shenzhen. I did not find the outcome of that meeting.
- **Russia's delegation is not yet set.** A Russian diplomat said Russia yet to choose head of G20 delegation, while confirming Russia will take part at a high level. I found no report naming who will lead it.
- **Lavrov's most recent US trip was a different event.** He arrived Friday in the city of Atlanta in the US state of Georgia for the G20 foreign ministers' meeting on Oct 30–31. That trip is outside the question window and was not in Florida.
- **Visa friction was reported.** Russia's foreign ministry said issues securing visas for its delegation were only resolved at the last minute.
- **Political opposition in the US.** Some Republicans and European allies objected to the Atlanta trip. One congressman said Lavrov should not be allowed in the country.

**Scheduled before close**

- The only known scheduled Florida event in the window is the Dec 14–15 leaders' summit. I found no confirmed Florida-specific ministerial or bilateral meeting involving Lavrov in December.

**Base rates and precedent**

- **Putin's absence has been the norm.** Putin last attended a G20 summit in person in 2019, and he participated virtually in the 2023 summit hosted by India, while Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov attended in person on Russia's behalf. The same pattern held in 2022 and 2023, when Lavrov represented Russia.
- **Lavrov has been to the US several times.** He has traveled to the United States several times to attend sessions of the UN General Assembly. He also did not attend this year's UNGA? No: the source says Putin did not attend and Lavrov represented Russia instead. Lavrov was in New York for UNGA in September 2026.
- **Travel to NATO states is rare.** Lavrov has traveled very infrequently to NATO member states since Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022. Florida is in the US, which is a NATO member.

**How it resolves if nothing changes**

- If Putin does not attend and Russia sends a lower-level delegation, or Lavrov is not named to lead it, the question resolves **No**. No Florida trip by Lavrov is currently reported.
- If Putin attends, Lavrov would likely accompany him. Historically, however, Lavrov has not always been the accompanying official at summits, so this is an inference rather than a confirmed plan.
- If Russia sends Lavrov to lead the delegation to the Miami summit without Putin, the question resolves **Yes**. This is the main path to a Yes outcome and is not yet confirmed.
- The Atlanta trip and any later Washington or New York trips do not count, since they are not in Florida.

**What I could not find**

- The outcome of the Putin–Trump talks in Shenzhen.
- Russia's named delegation head for Miami.
- Any official confirmation of Lavrov's role in the December summit.

---
## Second research pass (base rate, primary source, the case against)
**Already decided?** No. Nothing I found shows the outcome is settled.

**Primary-source status (dated)**
- **Kremlin, Nov 24, 2026 (TASS):** No decision yet on whether Putin attends the Miami G20. Peskov had tied it to the Shenzhen talks. A decision on whether Russian President Vladimir Putin will attend the G20 summit in Miami has yet to be made.
- **Shenzhen, Nov 19:** The first rundown said the outcome was missing. Putin's own account is that Russia will send a high-level delegation to the December summit, but he said the situation in Russia would guide his decision on Miami.
- **Invitation:** Trump, however, has invited Putin to attend the Miami G20.
- **Summit dates:** The United States holds the G20 presidency and will host the leaders' summit in Miami on December 14 and 15. Those dates fall inside the window. I did not check g20.org directly.

**Base rate**
- Putin's pattern is absence. President Putin has skipped recent summits of the grouping because of an International Criminal Court warrant against him, and European members have said they do not want to share a room with him.
- Lavrov's US trips are few. He has nevertheless visited the United States several times since then to attend U.N. General Assembly sessions. The Atlanta trip (Oct 30–31, 2026) was a G20 ministerial. I found no count of his Florida visits, and I found no record of any.
- Wider context: Putin's 2025 Alaska summit was Putin's first visit to the United States since 2015.

**Strongest evidence against a Yes**
- Putin is still undecided, and his stated condition is domestic. A Putin visit is the main route to Lavrov in Florida. Without it, Russia would need to choose Lavrov to lead a Miami delegation, and nothing reported says it will.
- Russia's wording is "high level," not "foreign minister." Russia's Miami delegation head has not been named.
- Lavrov is under US sanctions, and the Atlanta trip drew objections from some Republicans and European allies. The State Department did not say whether a waiver was needed for Atlanta, so a second trip carries similar friction.
- Lavrov's Atlanta role was a ministerial. A leaders' summit is usually led by the leader, so a Lavrov-led delegation is less likely than a Putin visit with Lavrov attending.

**Errors in the first rundown**
- The UNGA line is garbled. Its own note of uncertainty should not be taken as a finding. A Sept 2026 UNGA meeting with Rubio is reported, which does not bear on Florida.
- The Wikipedia summit page lists Putin as Russia's leader. That is a template entry, not evidence of attendance.

**Could not find**
- The outcome of the Shenzhen talks beyond the statements above.
- Russia's Miami delegation head.
- Any official Florida-specific Lavrov event in December.
- A precise count of Lavrov's US visits since 2022.
- The g20.org official participant list.
